Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 5 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
No evidence of internal derangement.

TROUVAILLES:

Fluide :
Épanchement articulaire modéré avec épaississement synovial. Pas de kyste poplité.

Compartiment médial (ménisque, ligament collatéral, cartilage) :
Changement de signal dégénératif léger dans le ménisque médial.
Ligament collatéral médial sans particularité.
Amincissement avec des zones de fissures profondes sur la surface portante du cartilage fémoral. Pas d'œdème de la moelle osseuse sous-chondrale sous-jacente.

Compartiment latéral (ménisque, complexe ligamentaire collatéral, cartilage) :
La corne postérieure et le corps du ménisque latéral présentent une déchirure en forme d'anse de seau avec un fragment déplacé médialement. La corne antérieure résiduelle présente une déchirure horizontale.
Déchirure partielle de bas grade du ligament collatéral fibulaire proximal.
Amincissement diffus du cartilage tibial au niveau de la surface articulaire.

Compartiment intercondylaire (ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur) :
Normal.

Compartiment antérieur (mécanisme extenseur, cartilage, coussinet adipeux de Hoffa) :
Léger œdème dans le cartilage rotulien sans perte chondrale.
Tendons du quadriceps et de la rotule sans particularité.

Os :
Formation d'un kyste dégénératif sur le plateau tibial médial. De minuscules ostéophytes apparaissent au niveau du condyle fémoral médial.

Muscles et structures neurovasculaires :
Légère tendinose du tendon semi-tendineux sans atrophie musculaire.

CONCLUSION :
1. Déchirure en anse de seau déplacée du ménisque latéral impliquant sa corne postérieure et son corps. Déchirure horizontale de la corne antérieure résiduelle du ménisque latéral.
2. Déchirure partielle de bas grade du ligament collatéral fibulaire proximal.
3. Légère arthrose du compartiment médial avec chondrose légère à modérée. Léger amincissement du cartilage à la surface d'appui du compartiment latéral et léger œdème du cartilage rotulien sans perte chondrale.
4. Épanchement articulaire modéré avec synovite.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Fall onto left knee while downhill skiing 3 months ago. Immediate bruising. Has had residual swelling and medial joint line pain. X-ray is negative for OA. Please evaluate for meniscal or ligamentous pathology.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Radial tear posterior horn and adjacent posterior root of the medial meniscus with slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

ACL, PCL MCL and LCL are intact.

MCL and LCL are intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.

Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament. No patellofemoral subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture peripheral weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle, measuring 8 mm anterior to posterior and 6 mm medial to lateral. Exuberant surrounding marrow edema. No evidence of displaced 1 stable osteochondral fragment.

Focal fissuring of articular cartilage central weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle as well as central to medial femoral trochlea and along the patellar apex and medial patellar facet.

Incidental finding 0.8 x 1.1 x 1.3 cm lowT1 signal intensity and high T2 signal intensity lesion, likely to represent an enchondroma.

3.5 x 1.3 x 2.7 cm the Baker's cyst. Trace fluid in the pes anserine bursa.

Small volume joint effusion.

INTERPRETATION:

1. Radial tear posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus slight extrusion. 
2. Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.
3. Medial femorotibial and patellofemoral chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment suggesting evolving mild patellofemoral predominant osteoarthritis of the left knee. 
4. Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament without patellofemoral subluxation. 
5. Mild pes anserine bursitis.
6. Incidental finding of enchondroma.

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. There is truncation of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with a fragment flipped posteriorly. Normal medial meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL. There is thickening of the femoral attachment of PCL suggesting previous sprain. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is minor thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is normal. Normal patellofemoral articulation.  
Conclusion: Flipped tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Mild knee effusion. No significant articular degeneration.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is large horizontal tear at the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is chronic partial tear (low grade) of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is anterior tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligamentous complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Large horizontal tear at the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
  Chronic partial tear (low grade) of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. There is horizontal tearing through the body of the lateral meniscus extending into the anterior horn. Horizontal tearing of the posterior body and posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus is also noted with a tiny para meniscal cyst formation.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning of the long medial compartment articular cartilage but no cartilage loss. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Mild - moderate patellofemoral degeneration also seen.  
Conclusion: Medial and lateral meniscal tearing. Patellofemoral and lateral compartment articular cartilage degeneration also noted.
